title: LinkedIn post (founder, company Page or document post)

gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, customer, quote, story or first-person experience that isn't in confirmed facts, founder material or cited research. Gaps are written around (pick an angle the confirmed facts fully support); never an invention, never a placeholder in publishable copy.

Limits and format: under 3,000 characters; the hook is complete within ~140 characters; 0-3 hashtags; no external link in the post body unless the brief requires it; at most one exclamation mark; no emoji bullets, headers or Unicode bold text.

Policy and platform safety: no engagement bait (Agree?, comment YES, like if, repost to help, polls for reach), no banned phrases from copy-fundamentals, no tagging or quoting people without confirmed permission, no fake screenshots or stock people presented as customers or staff.

anchors.1: Starts with an announcement ("I'm excited to..."), a generic truth or a feature line.
anchors.3: Clear topic but no tension, number or scene; a reader could skip it without curiosity.
anchors.5: Specific number, scene or tension in under ~140 characters that compels "see more" and is fully paid off by the body.

anchors.1: Opinion or advice with no basis in the author's experience or data.
anchors.3: Some experience shown, but details are ones any practitioner could write.
anchors.5: First-hand operational detail (a real number, decision, mistake or customer exchange) only this author or business could know.

anchors.1: Wall of text, or one-line broetry where each line is a standalone slogan.
anchors.3: Readable short paragraphs, but some could be removed without breaking anything.
anchors.5: Short paragraphs that form one cause-and-effect argument; removing any paragraph breaks what follows.

anchors.1: No numbers, names or mechanism; claims unsupported.
anchors.3: Some specifics but the central claim lacks proof or the proof arrives only at the end.
anchors.5: Central claim carries a confirmed number, customer phrase or mechanism by the middle of the post; nothing vague survives.

anchors.1: Off-positioning or generic category talk; no reader identifiable.
anchors.3: On-topic for the business but doesn't express a specific pillar, objection, alternative or trigger.
anchors.5: Expresses one positioning element for the best-fit reader, in their own words (VoC), without positioning jargon.

anchors.1: Ends in a moral, a pitch or bait; nothing for peers to add.
anchors.3: A takeaway that invites generic agreement, or a closing question anyone could answer with "yes".
anchors.5: An actionable takeaway plus a close that gives peers something substantive to add or dispute from their own experience.

anchors.1: Reads as an ad: feature list, pricing, "DM me for a demo" as the point.
anchors.3: Product mentioned naturally but more than once, or before the lesson lands.
anchors.5: Product appears at most once as the consequence of the lesson (founder post), or through a concrete asset (Page post), or not at all.

anchors.1: Corporate or AI-sounding: hype words, framework seams, uniform sentences.
anchors.3: Clean but could be any founder or brand.
anchors.5: Sounds like this specific person or brand talking to a peer; varied rhythm; matches voice samples.

anchors.1: No visual decision, or a stock/fake image; no alt text; hashtags not readable by screen readers.
anchors.3: A sensible visual or text-only choice, but the brief or alt text is vague.
anchors.5: Deliberate choice (text-only, real photo, document or captioned video) with a producible brief, descriptive alt text, CamelCase hashtags; document posts repeat the key point in the post text.
